For this study these were: turning at minimum every two hours; a minimum turn angle of 20°; with at least 15 min of tissue depressurization– which was a dynamic target. For example, if a patient stayed on his/her newly turned side for half of the minimum expected depressurization time (e.g. seven and half minutes vs. fifteen minutes), then the time-to-next turn was proportionally adjusted (i.e., turn time would be reduced by 50%, such that a turn would be required within one hour instead of two hours). This was performed continuously to achieve at least 15 min of cumulative tissue depressurization time every two hours” (p 14)

Char: Interventions:
Aim(s): “This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of micromovement strategies in posterior lumbar surgery, especially for overweight patients, to provide more scientific and practical preventive measures.”

Group A: (Experimental group: Micromovement group)

  • Received comprehensive intraoperative positioning on a one-piece prone pad with standard pressure injury prevention protocol based on the CORN PI risk scale
  • Head positioned on U-shaped silicone gel pad to avoid facial compression; arms curved and supported, abdomen suspended, hips on memory foam, knees padded, feet lifted off table
  • Micromovement protocol: 1 hour after surgical start, operating table tilted 15° to left for 5 minutes (under supervision), then 2 hours later tilted 15° to right. Operating table tilts alternated every 2 hours until end of surgery. Registered in a micro-movement log

Quote: “The micro‑movement group had regular adjustments to the operating table to change the patient’s position and alleviate pressure”

Group B: (Control: Multi-layer silicone foam group)

  • Same intraoperative positioning and prevention protocol based on the CORN PI risk scale.
  • Identical positioning: U-shaped silicone head pad, arm boards, memory foam hip pad, knee and foot offloading, soft straps to stabilise shoulders/knees, silicone foam dressing over hip bones
  • No micromovement. Patient remained in prone position for duration of surgery. Bed kept level throughout

Char: Participants:

Consecutive adult patients admitted to ICU with ARDS were included (n = 152). After 24-hours of mechanical ventialtion, 116 patients met the criteria for ARDS (intervention: n = 56; control: n = 60) and their eligibility was reconfirmed prior to formal enrollment and randomisation

Inclusion criteria:

  • all included patients had an artificial airway (either endotracheal intubation or tracheostomy), were undergoing mechanical ventilation for at least 36 hours, and demonstrated hemodynamic stability, defined as:
  • mean arterial pressure (MAP) ≥ 65 mmHg,
  • heart rate ≤ 100 beats/min,
  • noradrenaline (norepinephrine) dose ≤ 0.5 μg·kg⁻¹·min⁻¹, or Dopamine ≤ 15 μg·kg⁻¹·min⁻¹, or Epinephrine ≤ 0.2 μg·kg⁻¹·min⁻¹

Exclusion criteria:

  • hemodynamic instability (not meeting the above criteria)
  • intracranial hypertension
  • active acute bleeding
  • spinal cord injury
  • orthopedic surgery
  • recent abdominal surgery
  • severe pneumothorax
  • pregnancy

Immediate removal from prone positioning: 

  • cardiac arrest
  • major airway obstruction
  • dislodgement or displacement of the artificial airway
  • artificial airway obstruction
  • hemoptysis
  • central venous oxygen saturation (ScvO₂) < 60%
  • mean arterial pressure (MAP) < 60 mmHg, or a decrease in systolic blood pressure by more than 30 mmHg
  • heart rate increase > 20 beats/min or decrease > 5 beats/min
  • bradycardia < 30 beats/min sustained for 1 minute
  • SpO₂ < 85% or PaO₂ < 55 mmHg while receiving FiO₂ of 100%
  • evidence of barotrauma
  • development of pressure injuries
  • Or if the attending physician determined that immediate termination was clinically necessary.
